title: Garnet Systems Renewal & EU On‑Prem Activation Readout
summary: Garnet called to align on renewal terms, confirm EU on‑prem activation timeline, and scope dedicated capacity + burst behavior. Security gating (HSM/KMS, SOC2 evidence) and benchmark plan for latency/cost were primary blockers before SOW. SE offered a short pilot + synthetic benchmark run in Dublin racks. Next steps agreed: send SOW draft and security pack, run perf baseline, confirm hardware/HSM requirements.
topics: Capacity uplift in EU (Dublin) and burst into APAC
Private on‑prem activation - HSM/KMS integration and audit evidence
Dedicated capacity sizing and cost assumptions
Pilot benchmarks, test prompts, and success criteria
Contract extension length and SLA credits

Priya Malhotra: Run initial perf baseline on equivalent model in our Dublin test cluster and share results — due 2025-02-07
Marcus Li: Provide SOC2 + ISO27001 attestation and network architecture notes to Sofia — due 2025-02-02

Schedule 2-hour pilot kickoff (SE + Garnet infra) week of 2025-02-10

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-01-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47 mins | Attendees: Jordan H., Priya M., Marcus L. (Redwood) — Liam O'C., Sofia M., Haruto T., Elena R. (Garnet)

Summary (auto-gen, imperfect): Align on renewal and EU on-prem rollout. Discuss dedicated capacity sizing vs hosted burst. Security gate - HSM/KMS and SOC2 evidence. Plan pilot benchmarks.

[00:00] Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick rollcall — Jordan from Redwood here, Priya our SE, Marcus our CSM — thanks Garnet team for making time.
[00:12] Liam O'Connor: Yep, hi all. Liam here. We've got a bit to cover — renewal terms and the on‑prem activation in Dublin.
[00:20] Sofia Moreno: Sofia — security. I'll be focusing on KMS/HSM details and audit docs.
[00:27] Jordan Hayes: Great. Goal for today is to make sure we unblock the purchase decision, confirm the pilot and the timeline, and surface any last security or infra gaps.
[00:36] Haruto Tanaka: Quick note — our infra lead Haruto, we need the exact list of hardware plus HSM type. We run a hybrid rack set and want to avoid surprises.
[00:45] Priya Malhotra: Totally. Priya — from the SE side, we've been prepping a short benchmark and a config template for on‑prem. We'll map the model size, token profile and the batching to expected throughput.
[00:55] Elena Rossi: From product, Elena — our timeline is tight, we want EU activation + capacity uplift by end of March if possible, but procurement needs a clean security pass.

[01:10] Jordan Hayes: Okay real quick on pricing posture: the renewal we've proposed is a 12‑month extension with a committed Dedicated pool in the Ireland region, plus a small burst buffer to hit APAC for low‑latency users. We offered a three‑tier commit — small/medium/large — with step‑down unit pricing. Any immediate red flags?
[01:30] Liam O'Connor: The burst into APAC is attractive but we need clarity on cross‑region egress costs and fallback. Also, the KMS/HSM integration — are we talking Redwood‑managed keys or customer‑managed HSM?
[01:45] Marcus Li: Marcus here — we support customer‑managed KMS and HSM integrations. For Private/on‑prem, keys can remain in your HSM. We provide hooks and key rotation guidance. We'll need to document final network flows for your audits.
[02:05] Sofia Moreno: And do you have SOC2 evidence for the on‑prem control plane? We can't share secrets unless we have that attestation and penetration test summary.
[02:18] Jordan Hayes: Yes — we have SOC2 Type II for the hosted control plane. For Private deployments we supply architecture diagrams and third‑party attestation evidence; for the on‑prem package we can provide an audit pack. I'll have Marcus share the docs.
[02:32] Haruto Tanaka: On the infra sizing — if we pick the medium commit, what latency SLOs should we expect for a 2k token prompt with our existing model choices? We need 95th percentile under 300ms ideally.
[02:50] Priya Malhotra: That one's tricky. If you run quantized model variants and use prefix caching we can hit ~250–350ms p95 depending on batch size. If the sequence variability is high you might see spikes. Our recommendation is dedicated pool with continuous batching tuned to your token distribution.
[03:10] Elena Rossi: We're running 30% long sequences (4k tokens-ish) on average; that worries me.
[03:19] Priya Malhotra: Right — long tails change kernel selection. We'll trial a model variant with KV cache enabled; note sometimes the transcription or docs show KV as 'KV cash' in quick notes, but it's KV cache.
[03:35] Jordan Hayes: (laughs) yes, KV cache. Piloting will give a concrete baseline. Priya, can we run a synthetic test that mirrors Garnet's prompt mix?
[03:45] Priya Malhotra: Absolutely. If Liam can send 8–12 representative prompts and token histograms we'll run a 24–48 hour baseline in our Dublin test cluster and share p50/p95/p99 plus cost per 1k tokens estimates.
[04:00] Liam O'Connor: We can do that. We'll anonymize data but preserve length distributions.

[04:20] Sofia Moreno: About HSM, we run an on‑prem Thales Luna. Are there certs for that in your integration guide?
[04:28] Marcus Li: We have integrations documented for the common HSM vendors; Priya will follow up with the HSM key ceremony doc. If you need a custom adapter we'll scope it during the pilot.
[04:42] Haruto Tanaka: Network: do we need to open outbound to Redwood control plane? We try to avoid outbound 0.0.0.0 rules.
[04:52] Jordan Hayes: For private on‑prem there's an option for an air‑gapped control plane or a customer‑managed control plane — depends on the package. The typical VPC option needs only specific egress hosts and ports, documented in the onboarding guide. We'll confirm the exact IP ranges.
[05:12] Elena Rossi: Procurement will ask about SLA credits for latency breaches. Our legal wants a 99.9% up‑time SLA and credits for p95 latency above agreed thresholds. Is that possible?
[05:25] Jordan Hayes: We do SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated. Latency SLAs are negotiable for enterprise SOWs; we'll include an appendix with SLOs and remediation/credits.
[05:36] Liam O'Connor: Good. On pricing — the step tiers are coarse. Can we get an uplift cushion for short‑term bursts? Our traffic is seasonal.
[05:45] Jordan Hayes: We can include a 15% burst buffer for the first quarter after renewal as a one‑time benefit, and offer a path to autoscale more capacity with notice.

[06:10] Priya Malhotra: Quick technical caveat — when we do private on‑prem we recommend using the quantized 8‑bit path for cost efficiency; but for some precision‑sensitive routes you might prefer FP16. We'll profile both in the pilot.
[06:25] Haruto Tanaka: Noted. We'll need to list which routes are precision‑sensitive.

[06:40] Jordan Hayes: Let's talk timeline. You want EU activation by end of March. Realistically pilot kickoff in mid‑Feb, two weeks of benchmarking, a provisioning window in early March, then full activation by late March. That maps to procurement by the end of February. Does that align with your constraints?
[07:00] Elena Rossi: Procurement is aligned to EOM Feb but will need the SOW and security pack to start the buying workflow.

[07:12] Liam O'Connor: One more question — competitor angle. We've been talking to Cloudzilla and ModelHub — both pitched cheaper per‑token but with less robust on‑prem support. What's your migration story? We can't be locked in.
[07:25] Jordan Hayes: We provide model version pinning and exportable KV snapshots, so migration is straightforward. We also provide tooling to export prompts/evals and baseline logs for audits. Not perfect but we design it to avoid lock‑in.

[07:43] Sofia Moreno: On compliance, can Redwood support a customer‑run key rotation schedule? Our policy requires rotation every 90 days.
[07:50] Marcus Li: Yes, customer‑managed keys can be rotated per your schedule; we provide rotation APIs and key revocation flows. We'll document the full sequence.

[08:05] Priya Malhotra: For the bench tests, we'll include cost/cost‑per‑token, latency buckets, and a small plugin to simulate KV cache hit rates; often folks overestimate cache efficiency so we want realistic numbers.
[08:20] Haruto Tanaka: Cache hit estimation is important — our dataset is multi‑tenant and cold starts are frequent.

[08:35] Jordan Hayes: Anything else blocking?
[08:38] Elena Rossi: Security evidence and HSM docs are blockers. Procurement needs them.
[08:42] Marcus Li: Noted — I'll upload the pack to your SFTP by Monday and cc Sofia.
[08:49] Liam O'Connor: And the SOW + pricing?
[08:51] Jordan Hayes: I'll send the SOW draft Monday as well.

[09:10] --- Mid‑call technical dive (approx 20 minutes) ---
[09:15] Priya Malhotra: (deep dive) If you look at our kernel selection logic, long sequences fall back to an attention kernel that favors lower memory copies but slightly higher latency; if you quantize and use an optimized kernel we can shave 30–40ms on p95 for 2k tokens. However, worst‑case 4k requests still drive up cost.
[09:40] Haruto Tanaka: So is there an automatic fallback to smaller model variants if load spikes?
[09:46] Priya Malhotra: Yes — smart routing can route to a cheaper variant in the same family and you define quality thresholds. There's also an automatic degrade policy if capacity is constrained.
[10:00] Liam O'Connor: How are rollouts handled for model updates?
[10:05] Priya Malhotra: Canary by traffic % and rollback hooks. We keep KV cache compatibility in mind for rolling versions. Sometimes the transcript reads 'KV cash' in quick notes, sorry.

[10:25] Jordan Hayes: Ok good. Closing segment — let's recap next steps and owners.
[10:30] Jordan Hayes: Action items — SOW, perf baseline, security pack, prompt sets. Pilot kickoff week of Feb 10th. Marcus will share SOC2 and docs.
[10:45] Sofia Moreno: Please include network egress IP range in the security pack.
[10:49] Marcus Li: Will do.
[10:52] Liam O'Connor: We can deliver prompts and histograms by Feb 4th.
[10:55] Jordan Hayes: Great. Any final questions?
[11:00] Elena Rossi: No, thanks.
[11:02] Jordan Hayes: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email tomorrow with the SOW draft and links.

(End of meeting)

Notes on transcript quality: some words mis‑recognized (KV cache -> KV cash, Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood Dedicate), occasional speaker attribution may be off — typical of automated meeting exports.
